summary: L-5 cab lookout of the 1930s in Skamania County, WA, now gone; sources disagree on removal versus destruction; drive-up site with a footing and anchor bolt left.

facts.status_note: Register says the cab was abandoned and then removed; Willhite reports a 1964 USGS party found the lookout house destroyed. A footing and anchor bolt remain.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Gifford Pinchot National Forest

visit.trail_note: Forest road to an old circular loop just below the site, then a 20-foot trail to the site (Willhite).

events.note: Panoramic photos from 1935 show a flagpole and some sheds
USGS party said the lookout house had been destroyed (Willhite); the register says the cab was abandoned and then removed, with no date

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was abandoned and then removed, Willhite reports a 1964 USGS party found the lookout house destroyed, and firelookout.com lists the cab as gone with no removal date. No source gives a removal date, so the story reports the disagreement rather than choosing one.

notes_for_editor: Three sources only; no staffing, fire or reason-for-building information was found, so none is in the story. The 1940 'Columbia National Forest' is a photo caption on the Willhite page; I did not verify the forest's naming history. No source states legal access status, so no access level is set and the record's 'access: unknown' stands. The one WebSearch returned only the Willhite page.
